a human trick.text: The cruellest ghost is the one somebody built. This fear lives in the gap between a legend and the hands that keep it going, a scheme or a con dressed up as the supernatural, and it belongs mostly to the early decades, with half its films made before 1960. In Chandanghat [Kumar hears a woman singing from the swamp at night|1962-bees-saal-baad], while the village swears a wronged girl's spirit killed his father and grandfather, and a man in Kumar's stolen coat dies beneath the same tree. Les Diaboliques, House on Haunted Hill, The Village and Housebound keep the trick alive.

being taken over.text: Being taken over is the fear of losing the last private place, your own body, to something that speaks with your mouth. It barely exists before 1960 and has climbed ever since, and it runs strongest in Southeast Asia, where nearly a third of the films carry it. In Georgetown the words 'help me' rise on [Regan's stomach from within|1973-the-exorcist]. In Dakar [the men who built the tower, lost on the crossing to Spain, return inside the bodies of the living|2019-atlantics], and in Adelaide [a party game with an embalmed hand lets a dead stranger into little Riley|2022-talk-to-me].

blood drinkers.text: Blood drinkers feed on closeness, needing to be near you, invited in, trusted with your neck. Their hunger peaks in the 1960s and 70s and has all but left the record since 2015, with two films in nearly a hundred and fifty. In Wisborg [Ellen reads that only a pure-hearted woman's blood, freely given, can hold Orlok|1922-nosferatu], and in a Serbian farmhouse [a dead child begs at the door to be let in|1963-black-sabbath]. In a Stockholm suburb in 1982 [Oskar and Eli tap coded messages through their shared wall|2008-let-the-right-one-in] while Håkan kills to bring Eli blood.

dangerous children.text: A child is the person we are built to protect, which is why a child who kills, or who is somehow no child at all, strikes so deep. Here the young are evil, monstrous or inhuman, born deformed or gathered into cults that kill. More than half of these films come from the 1960s and 70s, the years of Village of the Damned, The Other, It's Alive and Who Can Kill a Child?. The fear lingers through Children of the Corn and Pet Sematary, and returns in Vivarium and Gretel & Hansel.

death and fate.text: Some fears have no monster, only the sense that the end is already written. Death and fate come as premonition, a time loop, or the slow discovery that one's own death has already happened, and in this record they belong wholly to North America, Britain and Europe. In a Kent cottage, [Walter Craig tells the guests he has seen them all in a dream that ends in something awful|1945-dead-of-night]. In Venice, [John Baxter keeps glimpsing a small figure in a red coat|1973-don-t-look-now], and on Jersey [Grace Stewart finds an album of photographs of the dead|2001-the-others].

evil places.text: Some places want you: a house, a building or a whole world that is haunted, alive or built to kill, and the fear has held steady in every era of the record. At Hill House [the doors close on their own and words on a wall call Eleanor home|1963-the-haunting], and in a Japanese country house [a piano bites off fingers and a lamp swallows a flying kick|1977-house-hausu]. In New Orleans [Liza Merrill reopens a hotel that stands over one of the seven gates of hell|1981-the-beyond], and elsewhere [two men wake chained at opposite ends of a derelict bathroom|2004-saw].

impostors and doubles.text: The face is familiar and the person behind it is gone. Impostors and doubles turn recognition itself into dread, and the fear has grown steadily, with eight of its films made since 2015. In Antarctica the men face [an organism that can perfectly imitate any living thing|1982-the-thing], while in Florida [Lena finds her husband Kane at home a year after he vanished into the Shimmer|2018-annihilation], soon gravely ill. At a Swedish border post [Tina meets a stranger with a scar on his tailbone just like hers|2018-border], and he tells her she is a troll.

monsters and creatures.text: Monsters are life that should not exist, bodies with hungers of their own and no interest in ours, and the fear grew sharply after 2000, with most of its films made in the last quarter century. In Seoul [a creature born of the poisoned Han River carries young Hyun-seo down into the water|2006-the-host], and deep under the Appalachians [pale, blind creatures hunt Sarah and her friends by sound|2005-the-descent]. Ofelia is led to [the lair of the Pale Man, a monster that eats children|2006-pan-s-labyrinth], and over a California valley [animals vanish into a cloud that never moves|2022-nope].

nature turning on us.text: The natural world has no malice, which makes it worse when animals attack and the sea, the fog and the fungus turn hostile, and North America makes most of these films. In the outback [a giant razorback boar smashes through Jake Cullen's house and carries off his grandson|1984-razorback], and in Antonio Bay [a glowing fog rolls in from the sea carrying a drowned crew|1980-the-fog]. In the Tsitsikamma forest [mushrooms sprout from living flesh|2021-gaia], and long before them [Kong carries Ann Darrow into a jungle of living dinosaurs|1933-king-kong].

people in your own life.text: The worst danger is often the one who knows where you sleep, a partner, a parent, a sister or a friend, and the fear swells in recent years, with nineteen films since 2015. On a New England farm [grief, hunger and a missing silver cup turn a family against Thomasin|2015-the-witch], and underground in North Carolina [Juno admits she has led her friends into a cave no rescue party could find|2005-the-descent]. In a Korean country house [Su-mi finds bruises on her sister's arms and blames their stepmother|2003-a-tale-of-two-sisters], and in New York Irena's jealousy follows Alice through the dark.

people who kill.text: The most common threat in the record is a human being with a knife, a plan or an appetite, present in nearly a quarter of all the films and in close to two of every five from Continental Europe. In Haddonfield [Michael Myers shadows Laurie Strode through the day|1978-halloween] before moving from house to house after dark, and in a sorority house at Christmas [Jess learns the calls are coming from inside the house|1974-black-christmas]. At an Austrian lake house [a polite young man comes to the kitchen to borrow eggs|1997-funny-games], and in Asami's bare apartment a large sack moves.

powers of the mind.text: This threat is invisible and lives behind the eyes: a gift for moving things or reading thoughts, or a will strong enough to command another person to kill. A psychic power can be a burden as much as a weapon, and it often belongs to a child who never asked for it. The fear is rare, nine films in the whole record, reaching back to The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. It surfaces again in Carrie, Scanners and The Dead Zone, in Cure in 1997, and most recently in The Innocents of 2021.

science playing god.text: Science playing god is the fear of the clever hand that will not stop: the experiment, the made creature, the machine that wears a human face. It was strongest early, with six of its sixteen films made before 1960. On a South Seas island [Dr. Moreau surgically shapes animals into people in the House of Pain|1932-island-of-lost-souls], and the beast-men scatter at the crack of his whip while gentle Lota's fingernails turn back into claws. The line runs from Frankenstein and The Invisible Man through Re-Animator and Splice to M3GAN.

sickness and poison.text: Sickness is the enemy you breathe in, carried by a rat, a chimpanzee, a spore or an idea. Unusually for this record, it belongs more to Europe and Britain than to North America, and it is climbing, with eleven films since 2015. [Orlok's ship fills Wisborg with deaths blamed on a plague|1922-nosferatu]. In Cambridge [activists free a chimpanzee infected with rage|2002-28-days-later] and Jim wakes to empty London streets, while in the mountain village of Gokseong [a bizarre infection drives villagers to kill their own families|2016-the-wailing].

something unseen.text: The unseen presence never shows itself, so it can be anything, a force pressing close that the films never name or show. At Hill House [something pounds at the bedroom door at night|1963-the-haunting], and beneath Hanging Rock [both watches stop at noon and three girls walk in a trance into a crevice in the stone|1975-picnic-at-hanging-rock], with only Irma found. Aboard [the derelict Event Horizon, each of the crew begins to see the people they failed|1997-event-horizon], and the fear stays rare and scattered, ten films across six regions.

the body turning monstrous.text: This is the fear that the self is only a shell: bodies turn into beasts, mutate or rebuild themselves around a foreign part, and the fear vanishes from the record in the 1960s and 70s before returning in force. In New York [Irena believes she will become a panther if roused to passion|1942-cat-people], and never consummates her marriage. At a Malaysian girls' school [Zaffan's first period arrives, her skin breaks out and her nails start to fall away|2023-tiger-stripes]. The Wolf Man, The Fly, Ginger Snaps and The Substance carry it on.

the dead that rise.text: The dead that rise are the ones we buried coming back in the flesh, hungry, changed or refusing to stay down, and they peak in the 1980s and 90s. At a Pennsylvania graveside [Barbra and Johnny are attacked by a pale man in a tattered suit|1968-night-of-the-living-dead], and in a Moldavian crypt [drops of a doctor's blood fall onto the witch Asa and she wakes|1960-black-sunday]. On the express from Seoul [the dead surge through the carriages|2016-train-to-busan], and in a Hong Kong tower block [a sweet old widow pays a black magician to bring her dead husband back|2013-rigor-mortis].

the devil and dark gods.text: Behind many horrors stands something older and larger, a devil, a jinn or a forgotten god acting on its own behalf. It is the threat the Middle East and North Africa reach for most, in four of their seven films, and it has grown since 2015. In 1980s Tehran, as missiles fall, [a neighbour boy's tale of djinn who steal a beloved possession starts to seem true|2016-under-the-shadow]. In Tumbbad [Vinayak lowers himself on a rope to steal gold from the starving god Hastar|2018-tumbbad], and on a New England farm the twins insist [their billy goat, Black Phillip, talks to them|2015-the-witch].

the enemy within.text: The enemy within is the terror of your own mind: grief that will not lie down, guilt, madness, a hunger you are ashamed of. It is one of the most widespread fears in the record, present in roughly one film in seven. At Bly [Miss Giddens sees a man and a woman in the grounds that only she seems to notice|1961-the-innocents], and in Adelaide [the pop-up book Amelia tears up returns to her doorstep with new pages|2014-the-babadook]. At veterinary school [Justine's shameful hunger moves from raw chicken to her sister's severed finger|2016-raw], and at the Bates Motel shy Norman talks over supper about his ailing mother.

the group turns on you.text: The group that turns on you is a village, a cult or a congregation that has already decided what you are for. The fear has surged lately, with almost half its films made since 2015. On a remote Welsh island [a cult's founders swear that blood sacrifice made the barren soil fertile|2018-apostle]. In Harjosari [the villagers are cold, children are buried every day, and babies are born without skin|2019-impetigore], and in the Indonesian countryside [a fertility cult's price is the last child, and Ian turns seven in three days|2017-satan-s-slaves].

the powerful and their systems.text: The powerful harm by design, when a company, an army, a state or a wealthy family treats ordinary lives as raw material. Upstate, [a gathering of wealthy white guests quietly bids on Chris's photograph|2017-get-out], and on LV-426 Ripley learns that [the company man Burke sent the colonists to the alien eggs for profit|1986-aliens]. Genjūrō sails on to sell his pottery as [armies sweep through his village on Lake Biwa|1953-ugetsu], and in Seoul officials announce a deadly virus while Gang-du's daughter is trapped in the sewers.

the restless dead.text: The restless dead will not be finished with us: the wronged, the abandoned, the murdered, the ones left behind. The fear is most at home in Asia, carried by exactly half the East Asian films and more than half of those from South Asia. In Izu [Reiko Asakawa watches a videotape, the phone screeches, and her seven days begin|1998-ringu], and faces surface in Tun's photographs after [Jane runs over a young woman and he keeps her in the car|2004-shutter]. In Chanderi [men stay indoors after ten because a woman's spirit takes them|2018-stree], and in Guatemala an old dictator hears a woman weeping at night.

witchcraft and cursed things.text: Witchcraft turns harm into something that can be handed over: a spell, a talisman, a mirror, a reel of film. It has climbed across the century to appear in one film in five since 2015, and it runs especially strong in Southeast Asia. In Freiburg [Suzy learns her dance academy was founded by a woman said to be a witch|1977-suspiria], and elsewhere [Öznur turns to black magic and sets jinn upon Nisa|2014-siccin]. [A bagua mirror brings Joy Ramirez luck and takes a soul for every stroke of it|2004-feng-shui], and in a Pennsylvania attic Ellison Oswalt finds Super 8 reels of families being murdered.
